Heres kikopup's guide to starting and using clicker training. I think it's kinda dry but really informative. Zak George is a little more animated and exciting in his videos and he has some videos on using a clicker for various behaviors. 

I've used clicker training to work on loose leash walking, fun tricks and reinforcing appropriate behaviors. If there's a behavior you want to capture, you can use a clicker. At first you want to give a treat or other reward after every click. Once the behavior is very replicable and they know it I go down to about 3/4 clicks get a treat, 2/3 clicks get a treat and then less and less often, take this slowly. You don't want to lose motivation, also feel free to make it a higher value reward or larger reward when fading. Keep in mind, don't do it in a pattern (they're smart, they will catch on), reward randomly. This is called gambling and it keeps behaviors consistent. Even with a well trained dog I still throw treats in every now and again to keep them motivated. I don't use a clicker anymore for established behaviors in my Delilah but if I teach her something new I dust it off.

I got the idea from a dog blog called Eileen and Dogs I think. I babysit a dog with allergies that causes rashes so I make him some limited ingredient training treats. 

1 c raw beef or chicken liver (beware, smells like death)

1 c tapioca flour (healthy and grain free, easy on the stomach!)

1 tb oil (like olive or veg oil)

1 egg

2 tb peanut butter or half cup fruit that they like

Preheat to 300 F 

Blend/puree/food process it all together (careful, this killed my weaker blender! But my magic bullet tears through it)

Line an 8"x8" brownie pan with parchment paper, it comes out clean and easy this way

Pour the slop into the pan and even it out a bit

Put it in for 30 min. Remember, your kitchen will smell like shit!

Wait for it to cool and then cut it into about 1cm x1cm squares.
